prompt:
You are a formal verification assistant. The following Dafny program fails Dafny verification.

=== PROGRAM ===
method twoSum(nums: array<int>, target: int) returns (i: int, j: int)
  requires nums.Length > 1
  requires exists i,j::0 <= i < j < nums.Length &&  nums[i] + nums[j] == target
  ensures 0 <= i < j < nums.Length && nums[i] + nums[j] == target
  ensures forall ii,jj:: (0 <= ii < i && ii < jj < nums.Length)  ==> nums[ii] + nums[jj] != target
  ensures forall jj:: i < jj < j ==> nums[i] + nums[jj] != target
{
  var n := nums.Length;
  i := 0;
  j := 1;
  while i < n - 1
    invariant 0 <= i < j <= n
  {
    j := i + 1;
    while j < n
      invariant 0 <= i < j <= n
      invariant forall jj :: i < jj < j ==> nums[i] + nums[jj] != target
    {
      if nums[i] + nums[j] == target {
        return;
      }
      j := j + 1;
    }

    i := i + 1;
  }
}

=== DAFNY ERROR ===
program.dfy(7,0): Error: a postcondition could not be proved on this return path

program.dfy(4,21): Related location: this is the postcondition that could not be proved
  |
4 |   ensures 0 <= i < j < nums.Length && nums[i] + nums[j] == target
  |                      ^

program.dfy(20,8): Error: a postcondition could not be proved on this return path

program.dfy(5,10): Related location: this is the postcondition that could not be proved
  |
5 |   ensures forall ii,jj:: (0 <= ii < i && ii < jj < nums.Length)  ==> nums[ii] + nums[jj] != target
  |           ^^^^^^

Dafny program verifier finished with 1 verified, 2 errors

=== COUNTEREXAMPLE ===
For the error at line 7: At initial state: nums.Length = 8857, nums[1594] = 609, nums[1595] = 5853, nums[8856] = 8365, target = 6462. At a program state: n = 8857. At a program state: i = 0. At a program state: j = 1.
For the error at line 20: At initial state: nums.Length = 8859, nums[2409] = 609, nums[2410] = 5853, nums[815] = -1045, nums[816] = 7507, nums[817] = -1045, target = 6462. At a program state: n = 8859. At a program state: i = 0. At a program state: j = 1.

Analyze the failure and respond with ONLY a valid JSON object — no explanation, no markdown, no code fences. Use exactly this structure:

{
  "spec_element": "<one of: requires | invariant | ensures>",
  "proof_obligation": "<one of: initiation | preservation | bridge>",
  "diagnosis": "<explanation of what broke and why>",
  "repair": "<the corrected Dafny specification line that restores the intended behavior>"
}

Definitions:
- requires: the precondition that must hold before the method executes
- invariant: the loop invariant that must hold throughout the loop
- ensures: the postcondition that the method must guarantee on return
- initiation: the precondition does not establish the invariant at loop entry
- preservation: the loop body does not maintain the invariant
- bridge: the invariant and loop exit condition do not imply the postcondition
